newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end flat, focus on lower liners.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end flat, focus on lower liners.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares ended flat as market interest continued to focus on second- and third-liner stocks, dealers said.
Bargain hunting after falls this week lifted most shares from the lows set in early trading, they said.

"Sentiment improved a bit but there's still an uncertainty in the market. This is reflected in the volume," said an institutional dealer with a bank-backed brokerage. "The consolidation phase may not be over."
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 0.04 at 1,249.76, after hitting an early low of 1,242.83.
The small-capitalised Second Board index was up 2.95 points at 657.68.
A diplomatic row between Singapore and Malaysia over remarks made by Singapore's Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew was largely ignored by the market.

"I really don't think it's an issue," said Simon Maughan, head of research at brokers W.I. Carr in Kuala Lumpur. "The stock market does not really react to the squabbles between Malaysia and Singapore."
At the moment, investors are more worried about the possibility of a U.S. interest rate hike, dealers said.
